A_open.text: Sunday night. Midterms start in twelve hours. The library is a battlefield of snacks and panic.
Students sleep on beanbags. Someone built a fort of encyclopedias. One pair of earplugs is a relic.
Mrs. Alder, do you have anything on the Pumpkin Research Program?
...The archive has been closed since 1999. Quiet hours.
She said 'archive' like I'd asked about her private life.
Dad: Good luck on your midterms! Study hard! Don't eat anything glowing!
Don't eat anything glowing? How does he know about the glowing?
Brad: Dad, what was the Pumpkin Research Program?
Dad: Library closes at midnight, right? Better study! Love you!
He did it again. Fine. I'll find out myself.
Brad! I've got seventeen highlighters and a plan! Study group at eleven!
I'm not asleep. I'm resting my eyes. Aggressively.
No eating in the stacks, Ms. Grove. Mr. Bart, nor in the aisles.
Okay. Three hours until midnight. Midterm and mystery. Let's go.

B_slots.text: The wall clock reads nine. The library closes at midnight. Brad has three time slots.
Each slot: study or search. Study right twice to pass. Search twice to find a way in.
A crow flaps through the reading room, chased by Mrs. Alder with a rolled-up newspaper.
The crow drops a flashcard on Brad's table. It reads: Powerhouse of the cell? Back: PUMPKIN.
Even the crow has been talking to Jane.
The crow exits through a high window. Mrs. Alder turns to Brad. 'You did not see that.'

then.text: Brad knows exactly where the archive is, and has a decent idea how to get in.

else.text: The archive stays a locked door. Not tonight.

B_slots.text: Eleven o'clock. The crowd thins. Someone approaches Brad's table.

study_1.text: Brad opens his biology notes. In the margins, in Jane's handwriting: THIS WILL BE ON THE EXAM.
Flashcard: What is the powerhouse of the cell?

study_1.prompt: The powerhouse of the cell is...

do.text: Wrong. The nucleus is the brain. Brad underlines the right answer twice.
Correct! Brad feels powerful, and a little smug.
Jane's voice echoes in his head: 'A pumpkin.' It is not. It is not a pumpkin.

study_1.text: Jane slides a pink highlighter across the table, wearing a conspiratorial grin.
Use the good one. Don't tell the others I have a good one.

study_2.text: The midterm has a Local Knowledge section. Ravenwood is thorough about its own legend.
Flashcard: How many crows appear on the Ravenwood crest?

do.text: Wrong. Sandra's voice: 'One. It's smug.' Brad underlines the right answer twice.
Correct! One smug crow. Brad hears Sandra's voice and smiles.
Wrong. Seven would be a lot of crows. Even for Ravenwood.

study_3.text: Flashcard: In what year was Ravenwood College founded?

do.text: Correct! The year of the fountain, and the man who loved fountains.
Wrong. Not even close. Brad underlines the right answer twice.
Wrong. The college is old. The bunting is from 1980.

study_3.text: A brownie lands on the table. Georgia grins at him from behind a trolley.
Brain fuel. Eat it before Mrs. Alder sees.

inv_1.text: Brad checks the card catalog. Nothing under Pumpkin Research Program.
He wanders into the back stacks. At the end of a dim hall: a steel door marked ARCHIVE. LOCKED.
At the end of the hall, Patricia stands before the archive door, looking at it too long.
Brad ducks behind a shelf. When he peeks out, she is gone.

inv_2.text: A clipboard hangs beside the archive door: the sign-out sheet. Brad reads the last entries.
E. Peters, 1999. And, in fresh ink: P. Peters. Last Thursday.
Patricia was here. After the tart. What was she looking for?

inv_3.text: The archive door has two locks. One is ancient. The other is shiny and new.
Someone has been protecting this recently. Someone who didn't want it opened.
Some doors are locked for reasons.

C_j.text: Jane sets down two thermoses and a color-coded study plan. Brad's name is in a highlighter.
Mitochondria flashcards at eleven. Break at midnight. Panic at one.
Hour one: mitochondria. Hour two: cheese. Hour three: weeping.

then.text: You've been staring at the archive door all night. I'm not blind.
Mr. Pruitt, the janitor, buys pumpkins from Dad. He owes us. He has the key.

then.prompt: Jane offers you the key, and the study plan.

do.text: The archive can wait. Let's study.
You chose cell structure over a secret room. That's romantic, in a way.
They quiz each other until midnight. Brad understands mitochondria better than he ever has.
I'll cover you. Ten minutes. Go.
Ten minutes. And you didn't get it from me.
Find anything?
Yes. Not tonight, though. I need to think.
I won't ask. When you're ready.

else.text: They quiz each other until midnight. Jane's handwriting is cheerfully terrifying.
You're better at this than you think. Brad Bart, the unlikely biologist.

C_s.text: Sandra drags her beanbag next to Brad's table and sits upside down.
I made a list of things I hate about exams. Seven pages. Want to read it?
Item one: exams. Items two through forty: also exams.

then.text: You've been circling the archive like a moth. I've been watching.
I've wanted to open that door for three years.
She pulls a bobby pin from her hair and tilts her head at the lock.

then.prompt: Sandra is already kneeling at the lock.

do.text: Click. Click. A very satisfying click. The old lock gives way.
Ladies first.
The 'Halloween dance incident'. It's in my grandfather's ledger too.
Now we both know. You're stuck with me.
The sign says No Entry. Maybe we shouldn't.
Coward. Fine. I'll go alone. You study.
Ten minutes later, Sandra reappears, dusty and pleased.
Last page of the binder. 'PROGRAM TERMINATED. Cause: Halloween dance incident.'
The dance. Thank you for telling me.
You owe me a coffee. Black. Like my soul.

else.text: Quiz time. What year was the fountain built? Don't say 'when the man fell in.'
Sandra drills him until midnight. It's the best study session of his life.

C_g.text: A snack trolley rolls up. On it: brownies, chips, and a plate labeled FOCUS FUDGE (UNTESTED).
Brain food! For you! And for me!
Oh! Weirdest thing. A gentleman came into the cafe. Trench coat, huge sunglasses, a very fake mustache.
He bought twenty pumpkin pies and asked if any were from the back patch.
Exact change. Tipped in pumpkin seeds.
A man in a fake mustache, buying back-patch pumpkins?

do.text: I'll eat. Then I'll study.
They eat, laugh, and gossip. Georgia nudges the trolley and it rolls down the hall.

then.text: The trolley slams against the archive door. The old lock cracks. The door swings open.
Oops! I only wanted my trolley back!
Is that Gord? When he was young? He looks sad even then.

do.text: Georgia, I have a midterm in nine hours. Let's focus.
Fine. Focus. I'll eat a sad rice cake.
They study. Georgia tries very hard to be quiet, and mostly fails.

then.text: At the end of the dim hall, the archive door is ajar. A line of light shows beneath it.
Someone left it open.
Mr. Bart.
I trusted you with a half hour of honesty. You used it. And now I find you here.

else.text: I'm not angry. I'm... frightened. What are you doing in my mother's archive?

do.text: The note. The soil. Gord's promise. The binder. I want to understand.
My mother told me once: some honesty is a kindness. Some is a flood.
She resigned the week after the dance. She never spoke of it again.
Thank you for telling me. I think we're on the same side.
I got lost. Looking for the bathroom.
In a locked archive. At midnight. With a flashlight. Lost.
I won't press. But I know when I'm being lied to, Mr. Bart.
Someone left this in my jacket at Homecoming.
...That is Gordon's hand.
So he is trying to tell you. And he can't. I understand better than you think.

then.text: Mr. Bart. Go home. Sleep. You have a midterm in eight hours.

else.text: Patricia pauses at his table. She sits across from him, clipboard on her knee.
A study tip. The exam rewards understanding, not memorization. Mostly.
Ask me one question about the cell. I'll tell you if it's on the test.
It's the most useful hour of Brad's semester.

archive_scene.text: The archive is a narrow room of steel shelves and dust. Brad's flashlight sweeps the boxes.
One box is marked in faded block capitals: PUMPKIN RESEARCH PROGRAM.
Inside: a binder, a ledger, and a stack of photographs.
The first photo: a young, bearded Gord hugging a very large pumpkin.
The second: Brad's father, in the same boots, scowling at a pumpkin.
Dad looks exactly like I do when I'm hauling pumpkins.
The binder is titled: PROJECT HONEST HARVEST. Director: Dr. E. Peters. Researchers: G. McVine, D. Bart.
In the margin, in handwriting Brad knows from birthday cards: I HATE PUMPKINS. -D.
The observation log reads: 'Subjects exhibit uncontrolled candor after ingestion. Duration: ten minutes.'
Ten minutes. Gord said ten in his day.
The last page is a typed memo, stamped SEALED.
PROGRAM TERMINATED. Cause: Halloween dance incident. All samples sealed. Sample 7 retained by Dr. E. Peters.
Compound blooms under a Halloween full moon. Recommend permanent destruction.
The dance. The bloom. A Halloween full moon.
This year, Halloween is a full moon.
Taped inside the cover is one more photo: three young people laughing, arms around each other.
They were friends. Then something happened at a dance, and they pretended it never existed.

D_close.text: Monday morning. The midterm. Brad sits in the lecture hall with a pencil and four hours of sleep.

then.text: The questions are fair. The Local Knowledge section is a gift. Brad finishes with minutes to spare.
A week later, the result: B+. Under it, in neat handwriting: Good work, Mr. Bart. -P. Peters.

else.text: The questions are hard. The Local Knowledge section is cruel. Brad guesses, a lot.
A week later, the result: D-. Under it, in neat handwriting: See me. -P. Peters.

then.text: Beneath that, in smaller letters: Honesty also counts.
The dance. A Halloween full moon. Gord's promise. This is all going to come together on Halloween.

else.text: Still nothing about the dance. But something big is coming. I can feel it.

D_close.text: A week later, the quad. Everyone compares grades like survivors of a small, intellectual war.

then.text: Pizza at the farm tonight. Pass or fail. That's the rule.
I survived. You survived. Coffee. Black. On you.
Celebration cupcakes! Or consolation cupcakes! Same cupcakes!

else.text: Mr. Bart. Your result is on the board. Try not to look so worried.

D_close.text: Gord: SATURDAY. TOWN MARKET. YOU'RE SELLING. BRING CHARM.
Charm. I have charm. I think.
